memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"'But if they do not acquire the means to repay, what was sold will remain
in the possession of the buyer until the Year of Jubilee. It will be
returned in the Jubilee, and they can then go back to their property'"
- Lev 25:28 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Suppose the person never recovered financially. Suppose no relative could
help and their own situation never improved. Was there any hope? Yes. When
all else failed, the Jubilee itself would restore what was lost. The land
would come back, guaranteed, at the appointed time.

This is the safety net beneath the safety net. Human effort might fail. A
kinsman might be unavailable. Personal recovery might never come. But the
Jubilee did not depend on any of those. It was fixed by God, and it would
arrive.

Dear reader, there is deep comfort here for the person who has run out of
options. Perhaps you have tried everything to fix a situation and nothing
has worked. Perhaps no one has come to help. God has a restoration that
does not depend on your effort or on anyone else coming through.

For the believer, the great Jubilee is still ahead. Paul writes that
creation itself will be liberated from its bondage to decay and brought
into the freedom of the children of God (Rom 8:21). Revelation promises a
day when God will make all things new, wiping every tear (Rev 21:4-5).

Some losses will only be restored on that day. But that day is as fixed and
certain as Israel's Jubilee. It is coming, whatever fails in the meantime.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What loss am I waiting to see restored?
2. Do I trust God's final restoration even where earthly hope has failed?
3. How does the certainty of that day steady me now?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, when all my efforts fail, You have a restoration that cannot fail.
Anchor my hope in the day You will make all things new. Amen.
